name: obs-lifecycle-rule
question: Does an OBS bucket in ${region} take a lifecycle rule that expires objects after ${days} day(s) and read the rule back?
about: A bucket named after the project, a lifecycle rule that expires every object after one day, then the rule read back with GET /BUCKET?lifecycle. The OBS calls go through the key service as in obs-policy-deny. The read back checks the status only: the lab reads JSON answers and OBS answers this one in XML. Every step is to confirm live: see the notes.

days.help: the days after which objects expire, at most 7

steps.says: a bucket named after the project and the expiry
steps.name: ${name}
steps.confirm: the create and the find, as in obs-policy-deny

steps.says: a lifecycle rule that expires objects
steps.confirm: to confirm live and likely to fail: OBS takes PUT /BUCKET?lifecycle as XML with a Content-MD5 header (OTC OBS API reference, PUT Bucket lifecycle); the key service sends every body as JSON without that header; the step runs the shape of obs-policy-deny and says what OBS answers. A key service that sends an XML body is the owner's change
GET /BUCKET?lifecycle answers 200 with the rule in XML, 404 NoSuchLifecycleConfiguration without one; the days are not compared because the lab reads JSON only

bucket.confirm: DELETE /BUCKET of an empty bucket; the lifecycle rule goes with the bucket

kb.statement: An OBS bucket in ${region} takes a lifecycle rule that expires objects after ${days} day(s) and returns the rule on GET /BUCKET?lifecycle.
